what: Iron Mountain stores and manages business records. It began with physical document storage in warehouses and now also runs data centres, destroys and digitises documents, and recycles retired IT equipment.
customers: About 240,000 organisations including most of the Fortune 1000: banks, hospitals, law firms, governments and technology companies.
money: decommissioning and reselling retired IT equipment
moat: Boxes that customers pay to store but almost never remove, giving revenue that persists for decades at very low cost once the warehouse is built.
risks: Debt of about $21 billion against almost no cash
Data centre expansion is capital-intensive and competes with far larger operators
Net margin of about 2% is depressed by depreciation and interest
Physical records volumes decline slowly as companies digitise
opportunities: Revenue grew about 12% last year and about 11% a year over three years
Storage revenue rises with annual price increases on boxes already stored
Data centres and asset disposal grow much faster than the legacy business
watch: Data centre leasing signed and organic storage revenue growth.
